newsitem.title: POLAND: HSBC SEES WARSAW BOURSE AT 21,000 AT YEAR-END.
newsitem.headline: HSBC SEES WARSAW BOURSE AT 21,000 AT YEAR-END.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse's main WIG index should end this year at 21,000 points, HSBC James Capel in London said in a report dated April 8.
"Our year-end target for the WIG is 21,000, representing an upside potential from its current level of 23 percent in US dollar terms," the report said.
The WIG index closed at 16,244.7 points on April 8 and at 16,333.1 points on Thursday.

HSBC said the Polish equity market would be driven by a higher combination of liquidity, attractive valuation and improving company profitability, the latter helped by strong domestic demand and an economic recovery in Western Europe.

The report said that though 21,000 points would break the bourse's current all-time record set in March 1994, this year's growth would prove sustainable since this time around as demand was foreign as well as domestic-based.

Price-earnings ratios are also significantly lower than the market's approximate 50 of three years ago, HSBC said, saying its 1997 market p/e was 10.2. The main market closed on Thursday with a current p/e of 15.6.

HSBC said this year's privatisation issues and and the listing of the 15 National Investment Funds (NFI) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme would broaden the market and encourage a fresh inflow of cash.
HSBC's favourite stocks included Budimex , Exbud, Mostostal Krakow , Agros and Animex .
Among banks it liked BPH and BRE .
It said brewers Zywiec and Okocim could extend gains on speculation that respective strategic shareholders Heineken and Carlsberg would raise their stakes.

HSBC's recommended sector weightings were 28 percent for banking, 18 percent for construction, 17 percent for meat processing and food, 14 percent for chemicals, 12 percent for brewing, six percent for tyres and five percent for drugs.
